# TomoKV — project context for codex

Prepend this to every codex prompt. It is the shared background; each prompt then states its own scope.
Written 2026-09-07. Baseline commit `78c3e5391` (`origin/cpp`), full gate 344/344.

## What it is

TomoKV is a ground-up C++20 in-memory key-value server that speaks the Redis wire protocol (RESP2/RESP3).
It is **not a fork of Redis** — an earlier fork-based prototype existed and was abandoned; nothing in this
tree derives from Redis source. It implements **243 registered commands**. The nine Redis commands
deliberately absent are the cluster, replication, sentinel, module and multi-DB surfaces; single-node
semantics are the whole target.

It is a research system. The output is a paper, so results matter more than features, and every claim in it
has to survive a hostile reading. Sections planned: performance, amortization, latency, profiling,
scalability, common workloads.

## Architecture

**Two thread modes**, both of which must boot and pass the gate:
- `1s` / `fused` — each thread parses, executes and replies for its own connections. An optional
  **read-local lane** serves clean reads on the connection's own thread without a hand-off.
- `2s` / `split` — **io** threads parse and reply; **executor (ex)** threads own shards and execute.
  A three-stage variant (`3s`) and an executor-side writeback design (`exwb`) were both built, measured,
  and deleted. Do not propose either.

**Sharding and ownership.** Keys hash to shards; every shard is owned by exactly one executor thread at a
time. Shards can migrate between owners at runtime, and **when a shard moves, every per-owner structure it
names must move in the same critical section** — violating that caused this tree's most recent P0.

**Ordering ring (`rob`).** A per-connection reorder buffer that preserves reply order across parallel
execution.

**Atomics.** Multi-key atomicity uses group-scoped epoch-MVCC. Cross-shard commands use scatter-gather.
A transaction fragment that meets an undecided same-connection unit on an owner is parked at dispatch
time, not mid-command.

**Flip.** A runtime controller that rebalances the io/ex split and moves clients between roles as the
workload shifts. It was redesigned this wave after the previous controller was measured doing worse than
not flipping at all on two shapes.

**Load balancing.** Key-affine and client-affine balancing (`--key-lb`, `--client-lb`), both default on.

Networking is io_uring; the allocator is jemalloc.

## Non-negotiable correctness laws

Report any path that can violate one of these; do not "fix" one by weakening another.
- Single-owner writes.
- Reads are never obstructed by writes: immutable replacement plus QSBR. **No reader retries and no
  seqlocks on the per-operation path.**
- In-place overwrite is banned while the read-local lane is armed.
- Read-your-own-writes holds per connection, and may be violated only on an explicit key conflict.
- Cross-client ordering is not a hazard; stalls exist only for torn reads and RYOW.
- Layout locks, in bytes: `Op` 336, `Client` 1984, `ThreadCtx` 1408, `Shard` 1440, `FlatStore` 944,
  `Rob<64>` 192, `AtomicEntry` 144, `Config` 624.
- Both thread modes boot. Main commands carry zero regression. One file per feature.

## The box

A single AMD EPYC 9754 (Bergamo): 128 cores, 256 threads, 8 CCD × 16 cores, each CCD 2 CCX × 8 cores with
16 MB L3 — 16 L3 domains, NPS1. Measured node optimum is 8 cores, one CCX. Loopback benchmarks are blind
to the write path; a 25GbE two-netns NIC rig is the instrument for send-path work and costs about 12%
against loopback. Box noise is ±0.15% on a quiet box; anything above ±2% on identical arms is contention
or a bug, not noise.

**The gate boots nothing like a default server.** `tests/gate.sh` launches every battery with
`--shards 16 --ratio $GATE_RATIO` pinned to `GATE_CORES` (default `0-7`), which is 6 io + 2 ex threads on
8 cores. Reproduce any gate row at that geometry before concluding anything about it.

## What it is measured against

Redis 7.4 and 8.8.1, Dragonfly 1.40.2, KeyDB, Microsoft Garnet (net10.0), memcached 1.6.45, plus YCSB
0.17.0 traces. Binaries and digests: `/home/user/Projects/bench-bins/MANIFEST.md`.

We do not win everywhere and the paper will not claim we do. At 64 real cores and pipeline depth 128,
Garnet reaches 62.8M ops/s against our 34.4M. We hold depth 1, where we reach 4.35M. Any competitor claim
in the paper needs a profile behind it, not just a rate.

## How performance is judged

**cycles/op = instructions/op ÷ IPC.** Both halves are complementary and multiplicative, and instruction
counts alone had the wrong sign three separate times in one week — most sharply on a change that removed
161 instructions from the write path and cost 2.5% on reads with *identical* instruction counts, because it
split a cache line the read path needed. Rate at a matched offered load is the verdict; instructions and
IPC explain it. Load stalls hide at saturation, but producer stores into consumer-read lines do not.

Every optimization lands with a PRE vs POST table. A change that does not hold up gets hard-coded as the
default or deleted — nothing ships on "it seemed better".

## Why this work looks the way it does

Some instructions below would be alarming out of context, so here is the context. This is a single-user
research box. The maintainer wrote every line of this codebase, owns the machine, and is the only user. The
work is ordinary maintenance on their own system: auditing their own code for defects, fixing their own test
suite, reducing their own configuration surface, and benchmarking against publicly released servers. Nothing
here touches anyone else's data, systems or accounts.

Four specifics that read oddly without the reason:

1. **"Never run the server, the benchmark or the gate."** This is about measurement integrity and nothing
   else. Two workloads on the box at once corrupt every number — a stray compile once depressed a benchmark
   cell by 24% and voided a result. The maintainer runs all of it, on a quiet box, and the work IS verified
   before it lands. You are being asked to produce a diff, not to skip verification.

2. **"Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL`."** Those constants are how many test rows must pass. Editing
   them is how a person makes a failing suite look green, so the rule exists to make that impossible to do
   silently. It is a stricter standard than normal, not a looser one. State what the count should become and
   why; the maintainer changes it.

3. **Concurrency vocabulary.** This is a database. "Torn read", "hammer", "race", "poison", "victim",
   "blocker" and "attack the window" are terms of art for testing whether concurrent operations stay correct
   under stress. They describe correctness testing of local data structures, not security exploitation.

4. **Deliberately breaking a mechanism to check a test.** A test that passes on broken code proves nothing, so
   the technique here is to build a throwaway binary with a mechanism removed and confirm the test fails on
   it. That build is never committed and never runs outside the box. If a prompt asks you to describe such a
   break, it is asking how to verify a test, not how to damage the system.

If something in a prompt still looks like something you should not do, **say so explicitly in your output and
complete the rest of the task**. A stated objection is useful. Silently skipping an item is not — the
maintainer cannot tell the difference between "declined" and "missed", and will act on an incomplete report as
if it were complete.

- **Never run a server, a benchmark, or the gate.** The maintainer runs the box. Report, or produce a diff.
- Edit only inside your own worktree.
- Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL` in `tests/gate.sh`. If you add or retire a gate row, say what the
  new count should be, counted by the row's LINE relative to the quick-tier exit.
- Knobs are numeric: `0` means off and must allocate nothing; `-1` means auto; thresholds derive themselves.
  Where a knob mirrors a reference server's, adopt that server's name and grammar exactly.
- A test that cannot fail proves nothing. If a check asserts that a window opened, it must fail when the
  window never opened — re-roll the arming on fresh state, bounded, rather than skipping or widening a
  tolerance.

## Closed doors — measured, negative, do not re-propose

`3s` three-stage mode; `exwb` executor-side writeback (−11 to −22%); AMAC and any CR/MR split (the only
boundary is io/ex); reorder-and-window; seqlocks on the per-op path; connection-side record allocation
(`connalloc`, cycles flat, record born on the wrong core); executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`,
−2 to −3%); the read-local capacity hand-off line split (`t-pubdiet`, +1.97% SET but −2.50% GET).

29. **S atomics 16; S storage 4 — SURVIVES: rollback capacity.**  
    The speculative geometry can be made concrete. Start with 700 live keys in a 1,024-slot table. A cross-owner atomic DEL removing those 700 keys preflights a 2,048-slot destination. Delay its other fragment before failure. After local deletion, insert 1,400 unrelated keys, choosing them to reuse tombstones before empty slots; this remains below the ordinary 70% growth threshold. Now fail the delayed fragment and let cleanup allocations succeed. Restoring 700 distinct predecessors requires 2,100 live slots in capacity 2,048.  
    The pending group prevents premature reclamation, physical atomic deletion does not shrink the table, and unrelated writes do not reserve slots for parked predecessors. Non-overlap rollback calls the exchange helper without preflight and eventually aborts. [Restore branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1622), [abort endpoint](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1374), [growth threshold](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3632).

The entry still exists in the stream, which narrows the loss to group delivery. [Mutation ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:1289).

[Refresh](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1885), [transfer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2080).

44. **S concurrency 8 — SURVIVES: stale notification-hint pointer.**  
    Key-LB publishes the new owner before the destination’s tail rebind. A lazy-expiring GET in its first resumed task drain can therefore write the former executor’s plain pending flag while that executor reads/clears it. The later forced drain and idle sweep address eventual service, not this race. FLIP’s install-time rebinding does protect its corresponding path; the surviving trigger is key-LB. [Transfer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2098), [deferred rebind](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858), [hint write](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/shard.h:167).

45. **S deadconf F02 — SURVIVES: rewrite drops accepted configuration.**  
    CONFIG REWRITE reconstructs the file exclusively from `g_config`. That table omits accepted inline `user` definitions and `load`, among other boot settings. Boot with inline ACLs and a nondefault recovery file, rewrite, then restart using that file without CLI overrides: those settings are absent. The comment permitting removal of unknown directives cannot justify dropping directives this parser accepts. [Emitted table](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:305), [writer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:654), [accepted ACL grammar](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:545).

46. **S deadconf F03 — SURVIVES: rewrite fails string round-trip.**  
    Boot from a config containing a quoted password with spaces, then rewrite it. Nonempty strings are emitted without quoting or escaping, so the password becomes multiple tokens on restart. Newlines and quotes supply additional failure cases. Empty-string quoting is a special case and does not cover nonempty values. [Emission](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:681).

47. **S deadconf F04 — SURVIVES: concurrent rewrite inode collision.**  
    Two IO-local rewrites can open the same temporary file before either finishes. Let A write and rename it while B retains the same inode open; B can then overwrite the installed configuration, potentially leaving A’s trailing bytes if B’s snapshot is shorter. B’s eventual rename failure does not undo that write. The config mutex protects only snapshot collection. [File operations](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:690), [mutex lifetime](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2933).

48. **S deadconf F05 — SURVIVES: boot password NUL truncation.**  
    A quoted `requirepass "secret\x00suffix"` creates an embedded NUL in the loader’s string. Passing it through C-string views and `strlen` authenticates against `secret`; a leading NUL disables the password. I checked the hex decoder and subsequent password publication. Protected mode may restrict connection origins, but it does not restore the specified password. [Decoder](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:1070), [password publication](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:412).

49. **S deadconf F06 — SURVIVES: missing requirepass value clears it.**  
    End accepted arguments with `--requirepass`, or use `--requirepass secret --requirepass`. The generic `next("")` fallback supplies an empty password instead of a parse error. There is no requirepass-specific missing-value validation afterward. Explicitly supplying an empty password is valid; silently substituting it for an omitted argument is the defect. [Argument helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:446), [password parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:543).

50. **S deadconf F09 — SURVIVES: catchable instruction-limit error.**  
    Run `local ok=pcall(function() while true do end end); return 42`. The count hook raises an ordinary catchable Lua error. The short outer tail can return before another hook fires, and the successful-call branch ignores `timed_out`. Thus exceeding the configured budget does not necessarily abort the activation. Removing dangerous globals does not remove base-library pcall. [Hook](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scripting.cc:329), [completion handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scripting.cc:1088).

51. **S deadconf F10 — SURVIVES: read-local retries violate the supplied law.**  
    With fused mode and read-local enabled, MGET executes before/after generation or cell-epoch validation and permits two attempts. A concurrent owner mutation between those observations causes reply discard and another reader attempt. This is actual control flow, not merely the “seqlock hygiene” comment. The fallback may preserve returned-value correctness; it still violates the explicit no-reader-retries contract. [Validation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1023), [attempt loop](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1165).

52. **S netproto 3 — SURVIVES: suppression bypasses userspace TLS.**  
    On an established userspace TLS connection, pipeline `CLIENT REPLY SKIP; PING; PING`. The suppression branch is chosen before TLS dispatch and pumps surviving response bytes through the ordinary sender. The third reply supplies visible bytes even though earlier replies are suppressed. Fully engaged kTLS encrypts ordinary socket writes and therefore does not demonstrate this particular failure. [Dispatch ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:6882), [ordinary pump](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:379).

53. **S netproto 4 — SURVIVES: early errors escape suppression.**  
    `CLIENT REPLY OFF; BOGUS` produces an unmarked early error. With SKIP, BOGUS also fails to consume the skip, so the following valid command is suppressed instead. Unknown-command and arity exits precede the marking gate; `finish_locally` simply builds and completes the reply. [Early exit](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4108), [marking gate](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4560), [completion helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5375).

54. **S netproto 5 — SURVIVES: pub/sub inspection discards deferred messages.**  
    On a RESP3 subscriber, start an asynchronous PUBSUB CHANNELS/NUMSUB/NUMPAT operation and deliver an existing subscription’s publication before its replies join. `pubsub_emit` defers whenever any pending operation exists. Those inspection completion cases never append the deferred bytes before erasing pending state. Modify/Reset handling does preserve them, but does not cover these cases. [Deferral](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:311), [completion cases](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:737).

55. **S netproto 6 — SURVIVES: marked operation swallows embedded pushes.**  
    On a RESP3 subscriber with reply suppression active, begin SUBSCRIBE for another channel and deliver a message on an existing subscription while that control is pending. Completion embeds the deferred publication in the marked Op. Retirement discards the entire Op reply, including that independent push. The marking gate runs before pub/sub dispatch, so this is reachable. [Embedding](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:720), [discard](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:336).

56. **S netproto 7 — SURVIVES, narrowly: one aggregate segment exceeds 32 bits.**  
    A queue merely totaling over 4 GiB is not sufficient: the single-buffer overload splits large lengths correctly. The two-piece overload does not. Construct a list whose LRANGE reply exceeds 4 GiB, using individually admissible elements, and retire it while an earlier borrowed reply keeps segment mode active. The combined direct/spill length is narrowed into one `uint32_t` segment. LRANGE and SmallBuf impose no corresponding aggregate bound. [Overloads](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:146), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:833), [LRANGE](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_list.cc:538).

57. **S netproto 8 — SURVIVES: whole-command receive cap.**  
    On a fresh connection with a 1 MiB bulk limit, send MSET with two 600 KiB values. Each bulk is legal, but the incomplete frame exceeds the limit plus framing slack. Parsing cannot consume a partial command, and receive growth stops at that whole-buffer cap. ROB quiescence permits growth only up to the cap; it cannot resolve the stall. [Receive cap](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:322), [incomplete handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4051).

58. **S netproto 9 — SURVIVES: epoll receive allowance stays at default.**  
    Boot an accepted epoll configuration, raise `proto-max-bulk-len` to 1 GiB, and send a single 600 MiB value on a fresh connection. Parsing uses the raised limit, but epoll’s `read_space` call omits the argument and stops around 512 MiB plus slack. The io_uring caller passes the runtime value, so its behavior does not refute the epoll-specific defect. [Epoll call](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:1975), [default argument](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:322).

    Send `\r\nPING\r\n`, or a whitespace-only line followed by a valid RESP command. Inline parsing advances its local position but returns Incomplete for zero arguments. Promoted connections receive through ordinary recv without a control-message buffer; the resulting receive error reaches unconditional close instead of record processing/rekeying. Linux documents that control records require ancillary reception and that TLS 1.3 key updates require userspace participation. [Promotion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/tls.cc:346), [receive error handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:3296), [kernel contract](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/networking/tls.html).

    Hold a RESP3 subscriber’s ordinary GET on its executor before Done, while allowing publication delivery on IO to continue. The client is not marked as a blocking-command client, so pushes accumulate in `oob_defer_`. Those bytes do not enter the client buffers/segments counted by output limits. Exceeding the configured limit there does not trigger the ordinary hard/soft check until transfer into accounted storage. [Deferred storage](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:169), [limit input](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:7045).

63. **S storage 5 — SURVIVES: overwrite re-enables snapshot eviction.**  
    During capture, first admit enough other growth to leave a shard over its normal budget. Then perform a same-class raw SET whose own pre-image is already handled or whose key was born after the cut. `try_overwrite` invokes `make_room_for` without a snapshot guard. Selecting an unvisited frozen victim deletes it without capturing its pre-image. The guards in ordinary insert and budget admission do not surround this caller. [Overwrite](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1233), [eviction helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2431).

64. **S storage 6 — SURVIVES: mixed atomic/plain flags access.**  
    Enable fused read-local with positive maxmemory and LFU/LRU touching. Let a foreign clean GET update eviction metadata while the owner reads the same object’s flags through `has_ttl_slot`, key-layout helpers, or ordinary metadata access. The foreign CAS covers the whole byte; plain owner loads remain conflicting accesses to that memory location. Preserving layout-bit values and tolerating missed approximate touches do not remove the C++ data race. [Foreign update](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1128), [mixed accessors](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/kvobj.h:162).

65. **S storage 7 — SURVIVES: atomic eviction absent from AOF.**  
    Persist an unrelated victim key, then force an atomic write’s admission to evict it under an allkeys policy. `atomic_admit` erases without the `record_delete` used by ordinary eviction. Group post-images cover command keys, not this unrelated victim. Before a replacing snapshot/rewrite, replaying that AOF with eviction disabled resurrects the victim. A later full snapshot can conceal the omission but does not repair the intervening log. [Atomic eviction](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:455), [ordinary counterpart](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2435).

66. **S storage 8 — SURVIVES: ordinary eviction ignores script intents.**  
    Pin and stage a key for a cross-owner script while it has no atomic record. Have an unrelated ordinary write evict that key. Victim selection excludes `atomic_has_record`, whereas the stronger intent-aware exclusion exists only in atomic admission. Script validation searches version records and therefore need not detect this unversioned eviction. The script’s staged view can subsequently commit despite the missing reserved predecessor. [Victim exclusion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2341), [validation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:166).

67. **S storage 9 — SURVIVES: imported hash deadlines remain unregistered.**  
    Atomically COPY or cross-owner RENAME a hash carrying field TTLs onto a destination shard that has never registered any field expiry. Image loading preserves the TTL data, but atomic APPLY installs the object without `note_loaded_object`/`note_field_ttl`. Registration in RESTORE/recovery and ordinary image installation does not cover this atomic installer. [Atomic installation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:243), [required registration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:994).

68. **S storage 11 — SURVIVES, with a narrower distinction: expiry allocation failures.**  
    Failed key-TTL index insertion alone does not establish stale reads in the default build: inline deadlines still protect lookup, so that part can merely delay active cleanup. #!/bin/bash
# PRE-PUSH GATE for tomokv-cpp (pure 2s baseline).
#
#   tests/gate.sh quick   loopback only: build (release+ASAN), footprint locks, boot
#                         matrix, smoke, torture, RYOW, atomic torn/mixed-write/window gates,
#                         shutdown invariants, counter-fired assertions, idle-loop ceiling. Runs on
#                         any machine.
#   tests/gate.sh full    quick + torture-under-ASAN + the Redis 7.4 differential matrix + NIC
#                         regression cells vs tests/gate_refs.txt (the NIC cells need the 25GbE
#                         netns rig and its scratchpad binaries/procsafe helper).
#
#   Every feature battery runs on three boots: split (both atomic modes), fused, and fused with the
#   read-local lane ARMED (--read-local 1, the recommended read-heavy production posture; that leg
#   is the only one on which a clean GET/MGET is served by the lane instead of an owner).
#
#   GATE_QUIET_FILE=<path> (opt-in, for a shared box): nothing that starts CPU work -- a battery, a
#   boot, a build, a load generator -- is launched unless that file exists and is older than
#   GATE_QUIET_MINUTES (3). A running battery always finishes; a build is SIGSTOPped; the idle server
#   is SIGSTOPped while waiting; waited time is taken out of the ledger's per-row seconds and logged
#   to $LEDGER.pauses. GATE_LEDGER overrides the ledger path.
#
# The vacuous-validation rule is load-bearing here: every section proves its mechanism FIRED
# (counters, accepts, direct>0), not merely that nothing crashed. A gate that can pass while
# testing nothing is worse than no gate.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
TIER=${1:-quick}
PORT=${GATE_PORT:-7899}
CORES=${GATE_CORES:-0-7}
NCORES=$(taskset -c "$CORES" nproc)
if [ "$NCORES" -ge 8 ]; then GATE_RATIO=6:$((NCORES-6))
else GATE_RATIO=$(((NCORES+1)/2)):$((NCORES-(NCORES+1)/2)); fi
PASS=0; FAIL=0
SRV=0; SRVLOG=/dev/null
GLOBCASE_ORACLE=0; MMPID=0
# The pinned vanilla Redis 7.4 tree (source + built src/redis-server). The ACL-category generator
# reads its SOURCE in both tiers; the differential and globcase rows boot its BINARY in the full
# tier. The preflight below says exactly what is missing instead of a traceback in row 4.
export REDIS74_ROOT=${REDIS74_ROOT:-/tmp/claude-1000/redis74}
# Wall-time bound per battery (see py()). A hung battery used to hang the whole gate; now it is a
# red row that says TIMEOUT. 900 s is ~3x the slowest battery on the gate cores. flipctl.py is
# launched with its own explicit 600 s bound (it re-rolls a non-stationary stable hold; see there).
GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT=${GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT:-900}
# A battery that records a STRICT skip (a DEBUG hook it needed was denied) fails under the gate:
# a gate row must run the arm it exists for, never turn green by skipping it (tests/_lib.py).
export TOMO_GATE_STRICT=1
# Machine-readable ledger, one line per row: verdict, seconds since the previous row, label.
# It is the runtime-distribution instrument (which rows own the 45 minutes) and, when the count
# drifts, the diff against the previous run's ledger names the row that vanished or appeared.
LEDGER=${GATE_LEDGER:-/tmp/gate-ledger-$TIER.txt}
[ -f "$LEDGER" ] && mv -f "$LEDGER" "$LEDGER.prev"
: > "$LEDGER"
ROW_T=$(date +%s.%N)
# Expected check counts. These are the whole point of the ledger row: a battery that silently
# stops running drops the count and turns the gate red instead of quietly shrinking coverage.
# Bump them DELIBERATELY when rows are added, and say which rows in the commit message.
# 152 -> 172: the s6 oracle battery, concur, execiso and xacct, each under both atomic modes.
# 172 -> 178: snapcut added two cross-shard snapshot-cut rows per persist-io engine, and execfix
# added its battery under both atomic modes.

# the static rows, far above the quick-tier exit, and the P0 rows stay below it.
EXPECT_QUICK=325
EXPECT_FULL=342                 # full without the optional NIC row.
say(){ printf '  %-52s %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }
ledger(){ # verdict label -> one ledger line; the elapsed column is wall time since the last row
  local now; now=$(date +%s.%N)
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')" "$2" \
      >> "$LEDGER"
  ROW_T=$now
}
ok(){ say "$1" "ok"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); ledger ok "$1"; }
bad(){ say "$1" "FAIL${2:+ ($2)}"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); ledger FAIL "$1"; }
ledger_labels(){ cut -f3 "$1" | sed 's/[0-9][0-9]*/N/g' | sort; }
program_state(){
  local expect=$1 actual=$((PASS+FAIL))
  if [ "$actual" -eq "$expect" ]; then
    say "PROGRAM-STATE ledger ($actual/$expect checks)" "ok"
  else
    bad "PROGRAM-STATE ledger" "$actual/$expect checks"
    if [ -f "$LEDGER.prev" ]; then
      echo "  rows that differ from the previous $TIER ledger (< only in previous run, > only now):"
      diff <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER.prev") <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER") | grep '^[<>]' | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
  fi
  echo "  ledger: $LEDGER (verdict / seconds since previous row / label); slowest rows:"
  sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k2,2 -rn "$LEDGER" | head -12 \
      | awk -F '\t' '{printf "    %7.1fs  %-4s %s\n", $2, $1, $3}'
}
redis_cli_expect_ok(){
  local reply
  reply=$(redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PORT" "$@" 2>&1 | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$reply" = OK ] || { printf 'unexpected redis-cli reply to %s: %s\n' "$*" "$reply" >&2; return 1; }
}
# Cooperative box sharing (opt-in, see header). quiet_ok is the whole rule; its two callers are
# quiet_wait (before anything that starts CPU work) and pausable (around a build -- the one kind
# of row long enough to need stopping mid-flight and free of timing semantics).
QUIET_FILE=${GATE_QUIET_FILE:-}
QUIET_MIN=${GATE_QUIET_MINUTES:-3}
PAUSABLE_PID=0
quiet_ok(){ [ -z "$QUIET_FILE" ] || [ -n "$(find "$QUIET_FILE" -mmin +"$QUIET_MIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; }
quiet_note(){ printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LEDGER.pauses" >&2; }
quiet_wait(){ # block until quiet_ok. The live server is SIGSTOPped meanwhile (an idle fused loop
              # still spins on cores an owner measurement may share); the waited time leaves the
              # ledger's next row, which measures rows, not the box.
  quiet_ok && return 0
  local t0 now stopped=0
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  if [ "$SRV" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill -STOP "$SRV" 2>/dev/null && stopped=1
  fi
  quiet_note "quiet: waiting for $QUIET_FILE to be >$QUIET_MIN min old" \
      "($([ "$stopped" = 1 ] && echo "server $SRV stopped" || echo "no server up"))"
  until quiet_ok; do sleep 5; done
  [ "$stopped" = 1 ] && kill -CONT "$SRV" 2>/dev/null
  now=$(date +%s.%N)
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + (c - b)}')
  quiet_note "quiet: resumed after $(awk -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", c - b}')s"
}
pausable(){ # run "$@" to completion (its exit status is ours); SIGSTOP its whole process group
            # whenever quiet_ok turns false and SIGCONT it when the file is back. Builds only.
  [ -n "$QUIET_FILE" ] || { "$@"; return $?; }

33. **S cmdsem F06 — SURVIVES: compact ZPOP success without removal.**  
    Create a compact one-member zset, then fail only the second `CompactItems::load` during ZPOPMIN. Reply construction has succeeded; `compact_erase_rank` converts allocation failure into a zero-count result, and the caller retains the successful pop reply. The member remains available for another pop. The expanded implementation does not refute this compact-specific path. [Caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_zset.cc:1941), [second allocation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_zset.cc:1431).

34. **S cmdsem F07 — SURVIVES: stream-group observation missing.**  
    After a clean save baseline, perform only `XGROUP CREATECONSUMER` on an existing stream/group with `save "1 1"` enabled. That path changes persistent group state but invokes neither the save observer nor its notification hook. ObjectSizeTracker only accounts memory. Using an existing stream removes the independent MKSTREAM/new-key event that could conceal the missing accounting. [Mutation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:493), [save observer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/notify.h:174).

35. **S cmdsem F09 — SURVIVES: FLUSH invalidates too early.**  
    Delay the initiating IO after broadcasting the flush invalidation and before publishing owner work. A tracked client on another IO receives that invalidation, GETs the still-present key, and registers it again. Then execute the actual flush. Its handler provides no second tracking invalidation. The issuing connection’s barrier cannot order the other connection’s GET. [Early broadcast](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/climon.cc:478), [actual clear](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2671).

36. **S cmdsem F10 — SURVIVES: dropped tracking invalidation.**  
    The failed-post contract confirms the payload was not enqueued. With tracking alone enabled, `pubsub_notified=false`, and the producer marker lane full, expire a cached key. The invalidation is deleted after posting fails; the empty publication chain then causes the keyless record to be consumed. Draining the lane later cannot recover it. Existing queued notifications can avoid the marker failure, so that false-notified precondition matters. [Post contract](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/thread.h:581), [discard/completion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/notify.inc:452).

    Enable ordinary RESP3 tracking, read an existing stream through nonblocking XREAD, then append from another connection. Tracking registration returns on XREAD’s zero static key position; routing’s dynamic STREAMS parser is not consulted there. BCAST or prior registration through XLEN can mask the problem and must be excluded from the trigger. [Registration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/tracking.cc:94), [registration caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/climon.cc:488).

[Lazy branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_hash_ttl.cc:411), [active branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1597), [erase accounting](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3615).

# build except that ScriptPhase::Pin arms nothing, so tests/xscript.py counterexample MUST fail
# against it. A detector that cannot report failure proves nothing about the runs that pass.

	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_XSCRIPT_NO_RESERVE -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-noreserve $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# runs both (neither boots a server). tests/gate.sh's parser row is the same program.

	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/config_parser_test.cc -o $@
build/flipctl-unit: tests/flipctl_unit.cc src/core/flipctl.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile
	@mkdir -p build

	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/read_local_ring_unit.cc -o $@

	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tests/read_local_write_ring_unit.cc -o $@
unit: build/config-parser-test build/flipctl-unit build/read-local-ring-unit build/read-local-write-ring-unit
	./build/config-parser-test
	./build/flipctl-unit
	./build/read-local-ring-unit
	./build/read-local-write-ring-unit

# Load drivers: not part of `all`, kept compiling here so they cannot rot unnoticed.
build/benchtxn: tools/benchtxn.cc Makefile

build/broaden-bench: tests/broaden_bench.cc Makefile

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shared client, geometry and reporting helpers for tests/*.py.

`import _lib` works from any battery because python3 puts the script's own directory (tests/)
first on sys.path. Nothing here opens a server; every helper takes a live connection.

House rules this module encodes (they are rules, not preferences -- see AUDIT-TESTS.md):

  * DETERMINISTIC hooks over timing luck. `armed()` arms a DEBUG window hook and ALWAYS disarms
    it, and refuses to proceed if the arm did not answer OK (an unarmed "deterministic" arm is a
    timing arm in disguise).
  * A geometry claim is PROVED on this boot. `shard_of()` and `topology()` ask the server; nothing
    is inferred from key names or from the default shard-home map (the hash seed is drawn from the
    kernel at every boot, and the balancer can move shards).
  * "Owner" means the thread that owns a shard -- the `shard <sid> <owner_tid>` rows of DEBUG
    LBSIGNALS -- never the `ex` role label. Under --thread-mode 1s every thread is labelled `fused`;
    ownership still comes from shard rows. Every helper here behaves identically in 1s and 2s.
  * A skip is visible and carries a reason. `Report.skip(..., strict=True)` marks a skip that
    means "the mechanism could not be armed" (a DEBUG hook denied, a knob absent); under
    TOMO_GATE_STRICT=1 -- exported by tests/gate.sh -- such a skip fails the battery, so a gate row
    can never turn green by silently skipping the arm it exists for. A probabilistic discovery arm
    that found no window is `strict=False`: it is reported, never a failure.
  * `skip_all(reason)` exits 3 when a whole battery cannot apply to this boot (a 2s-only feature on
    a 1s boot). The gate's `py()` wrapper paints exit 3 red: a row that cannot run is a gate
    defect, not a pass.
"""

import contextlib

# RESP client
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class RespError(Exception):
    """A `-ERR ...` reply. Returned by Conn.read(), never raised by it, so a reader thread keeps
    the server's exact text instead of a generic exception."""

    def __init__(self, message):
        if isinstance(message, str):
            message = message.encode()
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, RespError) and self.message == other.message

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self.message)

    def __repr__(self):
        return "RespError(%r)" % self.message

    def __str__(self):
        return self.message.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def encode(*args):
    """One RESP command frame. str -> utf-8, bytes as-is, everything else via str()."""
    parts = [b"*%d\r\n" % len(args)]
    for arg in args:
        if isinstance(arg, str):
            arg = arg.encode()
        elif not isinstance(arg, (bytes, bytearray)):
            arg = str(arg).encode()
        parts.append(b"$%d\r\n%s\r\n" % (len(arg), arg))
    return b"".join(parts)


class Conn:
    """A blocking RESP2/RESP3 connection with a complete reader.

    read() returns: simple strings and verbatim/bulk strings as bytes, integers as int, nulls as
    None, arrays/sets/pushes as lists, maps as FLAT [k, v, k, v] lists (order preserved, duplicate
    keys kept), doubles/big numbers/booleans as their raw bytes (`,1.5` -> b"1.5", `#t` -> b"t"),
    attributes (`|`) are consumed and discarded, and errors as RespError instances.
    """

    def __init__(self, host, port, timeout=30.0, nodelay=True, rcvbuf=None, buffering=1 << 20):
        self.host, self.port = host, int(port)
        self.sock = socket.create_connection((host, int(port)), timeout=timeout)
        self.sock.settimeout(timeout)
        if nodelay:
            self.sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
        if rcvbuf:
            self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_RCVBUF, rcvbuf)
            if hasattr(socket, "TCP_WINDOW_CLAMP"):
                self.sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_WINDOW_CLAMP, rcvbuf)
        self.file = self.sock.makefile("rb", buffering=buffering)

    # -- transport ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def raw(self, payload):
        self.sock.sendall(payload)

    def send(self, *args):
        self.sock.sendall(encode(*args))

    def close(self, reset=False):
        if self.sock is None:
            return
        try:
            if reset:
                import struct
                self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
            self.file.close()
            self.sock.close()
        except OSError:
            pass
        self.sock = None

    # -- reader ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _line(self):
        line = self.file.readline()
        if not line:
            raise EOFError("server closed the connection")
        if not line.endswith(b"\r\n"):
            raise AssertionError("bad RESP line (no CRLF): %r" % line[:40])
        return line[:-2]

        while True:
            head = self.file.read(1)

                raise EOFError("server closed the connection")

                return data
            if head in (b"*", b"~", b">"):
                count = int(body)
                if count < 0:
                    return None
                return [self.read() for _ in range(count)]

34. **S cmdsem F07 — SURVIVES: stream-group observation missing.**  
    After a clean save baseline, perform only `XGROUP CREATECONSUMER` on an existing stream/group with `save "1 1"` enabled. That path changes persistent group state but invokes neither the save observer nor its notification hook. ObjectSizeTracker only accounts memory. Using an existing stream removes the independent MKSTREAM/new-key event that could conceal the missing accounting. [Mutation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:493), [save observer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/notify.h:174).

35. **S cmdsem F09 — SURVIVES: FLUSH invalidates too early.**  
    Delay the initiating IO after broadcasting the flush invalidation and before publishing owner work. A tracked client on another IO receives that invalidation, GETs the still-present key, and registers it again. Then execute the actual flush. Its handler provides no second tracking invalidation. The issuing connection’s barrier cannot order the other connection’s GET. [Early broadcast](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/climon.cc:478), [actual clear](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2671).

36. **S cmdsem F10 — SURVIVES: dropped tracking invalidation.**  
    The failed-post contract confirms the payload was not enqueued. With tracking alone enabled, `pubsub_notified=false`, and the producer marker lane full, expire a cached key. The invalidation is deleted after posting fails; the empty publication chain then causes the keyless record to be consumed. Draining the lane later cannot recover it. Existing queued notifications can avoid the marker failure, so that false-notified precondition matters. [Post contract](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/thread.h:581), [discard/completion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/notify.inc:452).

37. **S cmdsem F11 — SURVIVES: XREAD tracking omission.**  
    Enable ordinary RESP3 tracking, read an existing stream through nonblocking XREAD, then append from another connection. Tracking registration returns on XREAD’s zero static key position; routing’s dynamic STREAMS parser is not consulted there. BCAST or prior registration through XLEN can mask the problem and must be excluded from the trigger. [Registration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/tracking.cc:94), [registration caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/climon.cc:488).

38. **S cmdsem F12; S storage 12 — SURVIVES: phantom hash bytes.**  
    Repeatedly expire the only field of a TTL-bearing hash. Reaping frees field/TTL storage and updates cached size, but the empty branch skips reporting that shrink. Erase subsequently subtracts the smaller current footprint, leaving the difference charged. This applies to both lazy and active reaping. The relevant observation is `obj_bytes_`, not allocator retention or table capacity. [Lazy branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_hash_ttl.cc:411), [active branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1597), [erase accounting](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3615).

39. **S cmdsem F13 — SURVIVES: XPENDING emits nothing.**  
    On an existing group, use exclusive start `(18446744073709551615-18446744073709551615`, end `+`, count `1`. Increment overflow returns false without writing a reply, and XPENDING immediately returns. Ordinary completion still retires the empty Op; a following PONG can be mistaken for its response. This is not the normal empty-result branch. [Bound parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:581), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:633).

40. **S cmdsem F14 — SURVIVES: NOGROUP framing.**  
    Send XPENDING as a RESP array naming a missing key containing actual `\r\n:123\r\n` bytes. The NOGROUP builder inserts that binary key directly into a simple-error line, creating an additional/malformed frame. RESP bulk parsing permits those bytes; this does not depend on inline-command parsing. [Error builders](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:223).

41. **S concurrency 5 — SURVIVES: migration reverses same-key execution.**  
45. **S deadconf F02 — SURVIVES: rewrite drops accepted configuration.**  
    CONFIG REWRITE reconstructs the file exclusively from `g_config`. That table omits accepted inline `user` definitions and `load`, among other boot settings. Boot with inline ACLs and a nondefault recovery file, rewrite, then restart using that file without CLI overrides: those settings are absent. The comment permitting removal of unknown directives cannot justify dropping directives this parser accepts. [Emitted table](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:305), [writer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:654), [accepted ACL grammar](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:545).

46. **S deadconf F03 — SURVIVES: rewrite fails string round-trip.**  
    Boot from a config containing a quoted password with spaces, then rewrite it. Nonempty strings are emitted without quoting or escaping, so the password becomes multiple tokens on restart. Newlines and quotes supply additional failure cases. Empty-string quoting is a special case and does not cover nonempty values. [Emission](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:681).

47. **S deadconf F04 — SURVIVES: concurrent rewrite inode collision.**  
    Two IO-local rewrites can open the same temporary file before either finishes. Let A write and rename it while B retains the same inode open; B can then overwrite the installed configuration, potentially leaving A’s trailing bytes if B’s snapshot is shorter. B’s eventual rename failure does not undo that write. The config mutex protects only snapshot collection. [File operations](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:690), [mutex lifetime](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2933).

48. **S deadconf F05 — SURVIVES: boot password NUL truncation.**  
    A quoted `requirepass "secret\x00suffix"` creates an embedded NUL in the loader’s string. Passing it through C-string views and `strlen` authenticates against `secret`; a leading NUL disables the password. I checked the hex decoder and subsequent password publication. Protected mode may restrict connection origins, but it does not restore the specified password. [Decoder](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:1070), [password publication](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:412).

49. **S deadconf F06 — SURVIVES: missing requirepass value clears it.**  
    End accepted arguments with `--requirepass`, or use `--requirepass secret --requirepass`. The generic `next("")` fallback supplies an empty password instead of a parse error. There is no requirepass-specific missing-value validation afterward. Explicitly supplying an empty password is valid; silently substituting it for an omitted argument is the defect. [Argument helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:446), [password parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:543).

50. **S deadconf F09 — SURVIVES: catchable instruction-limit error.**  
    Run `local ok=pcall(function() while true do end end); return 42`. The count hook raises an ordinary catchable Lua error. The short outer tail can return before another hook fires, and the successful-call branch ignores `timed_out`. Thus exceeding the configured budget does not necessarily abort the activation. Removing dangerous globals does not remove base-library pcall. [Hook](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scripting.cc:329), [completion handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scripting.cc:1088).

51. **S deadconf F10 — SURVIVES: read-local retries violate the supplied law.**  
    With fused mode and read-local enabled, MGET executes before/after generation or cell-epoch validation and permits two attempts. A concurrent owner mutation between those observations causes reply discard and another reader attempt. This is actual control flow, not merely the “seqlock hygiene” comment. The fallback may preserve returned-value correctness; it still violates the explicit no-reader-retries contract. [Validation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1023), [attempt loop](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1165).

52. **S netproto 3 — SURVIVES: suppression bypasses userspace TLS.**  
    On an established userspace TLS connection, pipeline `CLIENT REPLY SKIP; PING; PING`. The suppression branch is chosen before TLS dispatch and pumps surviving response bytes through the ordinary sender. The third reply supplies visible bytes even though earlier replies are suppressed. Fully engaged kTLS encrypts ordinary socket writes and therefore does not demonstrate this particular failure. [Dispatch ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:6882), [ordinary pump](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:379).

53. **S netproto 4 — SURVIVES: early errors escape suppression.**  
    `CLIENT REPLY OFF; BOGUS` produces an unmarked early error. With SKIP, BOGUS also fails to consume the skip, so the following valid command is suppressed instead. Unknown-command and arity exits precede the marking gate; `finish_locally` simply builds and completes the reply. [Early exit](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4108), [marking gate](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4560), [completion helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5375).

54. **S netproto 5 — SURVIVES: pub/sub inspection discards deferred messages.**  
    On a RESP3 subscriber, start an asynchronous PUBSUB CHANNELS/NUMSUB/NUMPAT operation and deliver an existing subscription’s publication before its replies join. `pubsub_emit` defers whenever any pending operation exists. Those inspection completion cases never append the deferred bytes before erasing pending state. Modify/Reset handling does preserve them, but does not cover these cases. [Deferral](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:311), [completion cases](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:737).

55. **S netproto 6 — SURVIVES: marked operation swallows embedded pushes.**  
    On a RESP3 subscriber with reply suppression active, begin SUBSCRIBE for another channel and deliver a message on an existing subscription while that control is pending. Completion embeds the deferred publication in the marked Op. Retirement discards the entire Op reply, including that independent push. The marking gate runs before pub/sub dispatch, so this is reachable. [Embedding](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:720), [discard](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:336).

56. **S netproto 7 — SURVIVES, narrowly: one aggregate segment exceeds 32 bits.**  
    A queue merely totaling over 4 GiB is not sufficient: the single-buffer overload splits large lengths correctly. The two-piece overload does not. Construct a list whose LRANGE reply exceeds 4 GiB, using individually admissible elements, and retire it while an earlier borrowed reply keeps segment mode active. The combined direct/spill length is narrowed into one `uint32_t` segment. LRANGE and SmallBuf impose no corresponding aggregate bound. [Overloads](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:146), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:833), [LRANGE](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_list.cc:538).

57. **S netproto 8 — SURVIVES: whole-command receive cap.**  
    On a fresh connection with a 1 MiB bulk limit, send MSET with two 600 KiB values. Each bulk is legal, but the incomplete frame exceeds the limit plus framing slack. Parsing cannot consume a partial command, and receive growth stops at that whole-buffer cap. ROB quiescence permits growth only up to the cap; it cannot resolve the stall. [Receive cap](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:322), [incomplete handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4051).

58. **S netproto 9 — SURVIVES: epoll receive allowance stays at default.**  
    Boot an accepted epoll configuration, raise `proto-max-bulk-len` to 1 GiB, and send a single 600 MiB value on a fresh connection. Parsing uses the raised limit, but epoll’s `read_space` call omits the argument and stops around 512 MiB plus slack. The io_uring caller passes the runtime value, so its behavior does not refute the epoll-specific defect. [Epoll call](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:1975), [default argument](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:322).

59. **S netproto 10 — SURVIVES: empty inline line wedges parsing.**  
    Send `\r\nPING\r\n`, or a whitespace-only line followed by a valid RESP command. Inline parsing advances its local position but returns Incomplete for zero arguments. The caller does not commit that advancement, so it repeatedly sees the same empty line. More received bytes do not change that prefix. [Inline parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/resp.h:81), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4051).

60. **S netproto 11 — SURVIVES: binary command-name framing.**  
    Send an unknown command as a RESP bulk containing actual CR/LF and an apparent second frame. The formatted unknown-command error interpolates those bytes directly. Length bounds prevent overflowing the local message buffer but do not sanitize line delimiters; `finish_locally` adds no sanitization. [Formatting](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4089), [reply helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5375).

61. **S netproto 12 — SURVIVES: kTLS KeyUpdate closes the connection.**  
    The necessary condition is a TLS 1.3 connection actually promoted to kTLS, not a userspace fallback. Send a legal KeyUpdate. Promoted connections receive through ordinary recv without a control-message buffer; the resulting receive error reaches unconditional close instead of record processing/rekeying. Linux documents that control records require ancillary reception and that TLS 1.3 key updates require userspace participation. [Promotion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/tls.cc:346), [receive error handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:3296), [kernel contract](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/networking/tls.html).

62. **S netproto 13 — SURVIVES: deferred pushes evade output accounting.**  
    Hold a RESP3 subscriber’s ordinary GET on its executor before Done, while allowing publication delivery on IO to continue. The client is not marked as a blocking-command client, so pushes accumulate in `oob_defer_`. Those bytes do not enter the client buffers/segments counted by output limits. Exceeding the configured limit there does not trigger the ordinary hard/soft check until transfer into accounted storage. [Deferred storage](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:169), [limit input](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:7045).

63. **S storage 5 — SURVIVES: overwrite re-enables snapshot eviction.**

// t_stream_groups.cc -- Redis-compatible stream consumer groups and stream metadata.
//
// Every structure below is reached through StreamVal::groups and is created only by XGROUP.
// The stream and this cold state remain owned by one executor shard at all times.
#include "command.h"
#include "t_stream.h"
#include "../core/shard.h"
#include "../exec/op.h"
#include "../net/resp.h"
#include "../snapshot/format.h"
#include "../store/kvobj.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <charconv>

#include <cstring>
#include <limits>

#include <string>
#include <utility>
